Container.Name: VaultS3
Container.Overview: S3-compatible object storage in one small binary, with a built-in web dashboard. Works with the AWS CLI, boto3, rclone, restic, Velero and any other S3 client.[br][br]Versioning and object lock, per-bucket encryption, quotas, lifecycle, IAM users and policies, replication to another site, scheduled backups and Prometheus metrics. Uses about 12 MiB of memory at idle. AGPL-3.0, no paid tier and no telemetry.[br][br]On the first start without a secret key, the server generates an admin secret and prints it once to the container log. The dashboard is at /dashboard/ on port 9000, which is also the S3 endpoint.
Container.Requires: VaultS3 5.0.13 or later. The container starts as root only to take ownership of its folders, then runs as PUID:PGID.

Config.Name: S3 API and dashboard
Config.Description: S3 endpoint, and the dashboard at /dashboard/.

Config.Name: Object data
Config.Description: Where the objects are stored. Put it on the share that should hold the data.

Config.Name: Metadata
Config.Description: The index of buckets, objects, users and keys. Small; keep it on a cache pool (SSD). Back it up together with the data.

Config.Name: Admin secret key
Config.Description: The admin's secret key; use a long random one. Leave empty to have one generated on the first start and printed once in the log. Once saved, change it from the dashboard; this field is then ignored.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: User the server runs as, and who owns the data and metadata folders. 99 is Unraid's nobody.

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: Group the server runs as. 100 is Unraid's users.

Config.Name: Buckets on first start
Config.Description: Comma-separated buckets to create if missing, e.g. backups,photos. Existing buckets are left alone.

Config.Name: Domain
Config.Description: Set for virtual-hosted bucket URLs (bucket.s3.example.com). Path-style URLs work without it.
